History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
32-year-old male with 2-month history of fatigue, poor sleep, low mood, decreased libido, and exertional shortness of breath; hypothyroidism on thyroxine; advised in-person review and blood work.

History:
• Main concerns: marked fatigue, difficulty getting up in the morning, low daytime energy, reduced appetite.  
• Onset/progression: Began approximately 2 months ago, coinciding with start of a new job; symptoms persistent.  
• Sleep: Troubled sleep; not waking early, but difficulty sleeping at all.  
• Mood/cognition: Feels distracted, decreased ability to focus, lower mood, no enjoyment loss reported in most activities. Denies suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.  
• Libido: Decreased over the same period; disinterested in sexual activity with spouse. No reported change in morning erections.  
• Other associated symptoms: Shortness of breath during sports over same timeframe.  
• No visual changes.  
• Systems review otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism – on long-term thyroxine therapy. No specific complications noted.

Medications:
• Thyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Married.  
• Started a new job 2 months ago.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, exercise habits, and occupational details not discussed.

Family History:
• Father committed suicide 15 years ago (psychiatric history).  
• Mother well; patient is an only child.  
• No other family history of depression or significant medical illness noted.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during video consult; no vitals documented.

Investigations:
• None completed yet; clinician plans blood tests (specific panels not detailed).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Fatigue, poor sleep, and exertional dyspnea
  • Differential includes uncontrolled/undertreated hypothyroidism, anemia, mood disorder, other endocrine or cardiorespiratory etiologies.
  • Plan:
    ‑ Arrange in-person GP appointment within a few days for full physical examination.  
    ‑ Order blood work (thyroid profile, CBC, metabolic panel, etc.) – specifics to be determined at visit.  

Issue 2: Low mood and decreased libido
  • Possible depressive episode; may relate to work stress or thyroid dysfunction.
  • Plan:
    ‑ Screen formally for depression/anxiety during in-person visit.  
    ‑ Assess impact on daily functioning and discuss management options after laboratory results.  
    ‑ Patient currently denies suicidal ideation; advise to seek urgent help if this changes.

Issue 3: Hypothyroidism (existing)
  • Need to rule out suboptimal control contributing to current symptoms.
  • Plan:
    ‑ Check TSH, free T4.  
    ‑ Review thyroxine dose adherence and timing once labs return.

General Plan Items:
• Provide patient with reassurance and explanation of next steps.  
• Encourage good sleep hygiene and regular meals pending review.  
• Safety-net: instructed to seek immediate medical attention for worsening symptoms or emergent concerns (e.g., suicidal thoughts, severe dyspnea).

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected: vitals, comprehensive ROS, smoking/alcohol history, medication dose & frequency, physical exam findings.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript clear; minor audio freeze noted but did not affect data capture.
